diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource is applied before this module is guaranteed to install the cert-manager and AWS PCA issuer charts/CRDs. Without waiting for the add-ons module, Kubernetes may reject the manifest because its custom resource definition is not yet registered.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The cluster_pca_issuer manifest creates an AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource, whose CRD is installed by the Kubernetes add-ons module (including the AWS Private CA issuer). Without this dependency, Terraform may apply the custom resource before that CRD exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The PCA certificate issuer is a custom resource, but its CRD is installed by the Kubernetes add-ons module. Without ordering, kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer may be applied before that chart/CRD exists; make it depend on the add-ons module.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies a manifest of kind AWSPCAClusterIssuer, a CRD installed by the aws-privateca-issuer add-on that is deployed via module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (enable_aws_privateca_issuer = true). The resource currently only depends on the eks_cluster_id output and the CA resource, so Terraform may apply it before the CRD/controller exists, causing an apply failure ("no matches for kind AWSPCAClusterIssuer"). It should depend on module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (as example_pca_certificate already does). No clean data-reference fix exists because that module exports no attribute referencing the CRD.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies an `AWSPCAClusterIssuer` custom resource, but that CRD is only installed by the cert-manager / aws-privateca-issuer Helm add-ons created in module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons. The manifest currently depends only on the EKS cluster (module.eks_blueprints) and the CA, so it can be applied before the CRD exists and fail. It should depend on module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (as example_pca_certificate already correctly does). No data reference is possible since that module exposes no outputs.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer creates an AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource, but it only depends on aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.example and the cluster id. The `awspca.cert-manager.io` CRD is installed by the aws-privateca-issuer add-on deployed by module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (enable_aws_privateca_issuer = true). Without an ordering dependency on that module, Terraform may try to apply the CR before the CRD exists, causing the apply to fail. The sibling kubectl_manifest.example_pca_certificate already depends on this module.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies an AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource, whose CRD is installed by the aws-privateca-issuer add-on inside module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons. The manifest only references aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.example.arn and the cluster id, so Terraform may attempt to apply it before cert-manager and the PCA issuer (and their CRDs) are deployed, failing the apply. It needs an explicit ordering dependency on the addons module (the sibling resource kubectl_manifest.example_pca_certificate already has this depends_on, but cluster_pca_issuer does not).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
resource.kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies a custom resource of kind AWSPCAClusterIssuer (awspca.cert-manager.io/v1beta1). That CRD is only installed by the aws-privateca-issuer Helm add-on deployed via module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons (which also installs cert-manager). Without waiting for that module, a fresh apply can attempt to create the cluster issuer before its CRD exists, failing with "no matches for kind AWSPCAClusterIssuer". It currently depends only on aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.example and the EKS cluster ID.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
`kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer` applies a custom resource of kind `AWSPCAClusterIssuer` (apiVersion `awspca.cert-manager.io/v1beta1`). This CRD is only defined once the cert-manager / aws-privateca-issuer add-ons from `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` have been installed (the aws-privateca-issuer Helm chart ships the AWSPCAClusterIssuer CRD). Without an ordering link, this manifest can be applied before the add-on stack exists and fail (the provider's apply retry can mask the timing only incidentally). The sibling resource `kubectl_manifest.example_pca_certificate` correctly carries `depends_on = [module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons, ...]`, but this issuer manifest does not.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The issuer manifest uses the PCA authority ARN while the authority is still in PENDING_CERTIFICATE until its certificate is associated. Ordering issuer creation after the authority-certificate association avoids configuring the issuer against a CA that cannot yet issue certificates.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The cluster_pca_issuer manifest configures an ACM PCA authority that is still in PENDING_CERTIFICATE until its CA certificate is associated. Its ARN reference only orders it after authority creation, not after activation; it should wait for the certificate association.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The PCA issuer manifest can be applied while the authority is still in PENDING_CERTIFICATE; the CA cannot issue certificates until its signed certificate is associated. Make this manifest wait for the CA certificate association resource.
